title: Signal fidelity retuning notes and postmortem (draft)
content:
Overview:

This is a working draft summarizing last week's incident where multiple SLO burn alerts and a cascade of noisy pagers masked the real signal: a partial exporter/telemetry pipeline degradation that caused metric drops and a downstream spike in error-rate calculations. Goal is to capture timeline, why observability failed us, and concrete retuning/runbook actions so oncall noise and future SLO flares are less likely.

High-level impact:
- Incident window: 2025-11-18 03:12 UTC -> 2025-11-18 07:40 UTC
- Services impacted: inference-router, kv-cache-proxy (user-facing latency & availability SLOs saw short burn)
- Pager volume: ~36 pages across 4 alerts (multiple duplicates due to high cardinality and lack of dedupe)
- Visible customer impact: transient increased 5xx rate and several timeouts (rbe up to 7m for small percentage of requests)

Timeline (abridged):
- 03:12 UTC: First SLO burn alert (latency_p95 > 1200ms) fires from hosted-api-prod
- 03:14 UTC: Multiple derived alerts fire (increase in 5xx rate, request_retry_rate) -> oncall paged
- 03:16 UTC: Oncall notices missing exporter metrics for kv-cache-proxy in telemetry dashboard (target disappeared from Prometheus)
- 03:22 UTC: Runbook followed to verify Prometheus targets; discovered exporter process on host had OOM-killed and restarted repeatedly
- 03:45 UTC: Engineering infra autoscaler restarted host; exporter resumed but with a degraded scrape cadence causing sparse samples
- 04:10 UTC: Alert storms continue because rolling windows counted previously missing samples as zero and derived rates spiked (slo-burn calc used count/s or error fraction computations that assumed continuous samples)
- 05:30 UTC: Patch deployed to exporter to reduce memory footprint; scrape stability improves
- 07:40 UTC: SLO burn resolved, alerts return to green

Key observations about observability failures:
1) Missing metrics were treated as zeros in derived alerts
   - Several alert rules compute error_budget burn by dividing error_count by request_count over 1m windows. When request_count went to zero (or was absent), rules treated that as 0 and error_rate math produced noisy spikes.
2) High cardinality alerts amplified noise
   - Alerts were defined per instance/container label without grouping; when exporter restarts happened they created transient label churn and produced one alert per container (~12x duplication). No grouping/deduping occurred in notification layer.
3) No heartbeat / exporter health metric to explicitly indicate scraping health
   - We only had to infer missingness by looking at target status; there is no standardized heartbeat metric per service to quickly differentiate missing telemetry from real production errors.
4) Alert windows too short for noisy signals
   - Many rules used 1m or 2m windows. Combined with scrapers that can miss samples for several minutes during restart, the aggregate metrics oscillated.
5) SLO computation assumptions mismatch with data availability
   - SLO query logic assumed continuous sampling; it did not handle NaN/missing gracefully. Where promql returns NaN or absent, alerting should ignore or backoff rather than treat as 0.

Root cause (summary):
- Primary: exporter memory leak in kv-cache-proxy image causing repeated OOM restarts on older hosts running an overloaded monitoring agent. This led to scrapes failing intermittently.
- Secondary: alerting rules and SLO queries made unsafe assumptions about metric availability (treated missing as zero).
- Tertiary: notification configuration lacked intelligent grouping/deduping and we had no synthetic heartbeat metric to quickly triage missing data vs real customer errors.

Why this created noisy pagers and prolonged SLO burns:
- Missing metrics -> derived calculations produced unexpected spikes
- Multiple per-instance alerts -> duplicate paging
- Short windows + scrape jitter -> flapping alerts not suppressed by alertmanager grouping
- Oncall had to manually triage exporter vs service issue because no dedicated runbook step existed for telemetry partial-degradation

Immediate remediation we executed:
- Rotated affected hosts out of the pool and redeployed exporter with a memory-fix (SRE + infra)
- Increased scrape timeout and reduced scrape concurrency temporarily to reduce pressure on monitoring agent
- Applied temporary silencing on duplicate per-instance alerts while root cause was addressed

Proposed long-term fixes (prioritized):
1) Add heartbeat metric for each service: service_metric_heartbeat{service,env} -> increments every 30s from exporter. Alert if absent for 3m+.
   - Owner: Priya Patel
   - Jira: SRE-1423
2) Change SLO alerting queries to be missing-safe and use rate() with fallback and ignore NaNs. Example promql pattern to consider:
   - error_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api"}[5m]))
   - Use clamp_min or coalesce patterns to avoid divide-by-zero: sum(rate(...)) / max(1e-6, sum(rate(...)))
   - Owner: Diego Ramos
3) Increase alert evaluation windows for derived SLO-burn rules to 5m min with a 2/3 evaluation hold (e.g., for 2 consecutive evals) to reduce flaps. Use forlatency and transient 1m signals keep short for immediate ops only.
   - Owner: Ava Chen
4) Implement notification grouping keys in Alertmanager and enable dedupe by service+region rather than instance to prevent 10x duplicate pagers.
   - Owner: SRE Ops
5) Add a specific runbook section "Telemetry missing -> verify heartbeat" that lists Prometheus targets page, exporter logs, host OOM logs, and escalation path to infra.
   - Owner: SRE oncall docs
6) Add synthetic canary traffic and a separate instrumentation pipeline for SLO-computation so missing telemetry does not directly feed noisy SLA calculations.
   - Owner: Platform Engineering

Detection/runbook snippets (for oncall):
1) Surface check: Go to Prometheus -> Targets -> filter for kv-cache-proxy: are targets UP? If target is absent or DOWN, proceed to step 2.
2) Heartbeat: query service_metric_heartbeat{service="kv-cache-proxy",env="prod"} for last 5m. If missing -> treat as telemetry outage, silence per-instance alerts and page infra.
3) Check exporter logs: ssh to host (listed on prometheus target) and run: sudo journalctl -u kv-cache-exporter -n 500 | grep -i oom
4) If exporter OOM'ed -> mark host for rotation, escalate to infra to restart agent/container; if repeated OOMs, collect core / pmap and open SRE-1423.
5) If targets are UP but metrics sparse: check node-exporter metrics, scrape_duration_seconds, and Prometheus scrape_samples_post_metric_relabeling for this target.

Sample Prometheus queries to help triage (copyable):
- Prometheus scrape target status: up{job="prometheus",instance=~"prometheus.*"} (then inspect metrics on /targets page)
- Exporter heartbeat (post-implementation): absent_over_time(service_metric_heartbeat{service="kv-cache-proxy"}[3m])
- Request vs error delta: sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="inference-router"}[5m])) by (instance) 
  vs sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="inference-router",code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)

Alert retuning checklist (short):
- [ ] Add heartbeat metric and alert
- [ ] Update SLO queries to guard for missing data
- [ ] Increase evaluation windows for derived alerts to >=5m where appropriate
- [ ] Switch per-instance notification key to service-level grouping
- [ ] Add suppression rules for canary labels and rollout labels
- [ ] Postmortem writeup and code PRs linking to SRE-1423 / infra fixes

Action items with owners & target dates:
- Priya: implement heartbeat + test in staging (due 2026-01-10)
- Diego: update SLO promql and open PR to alerting rules (due 2026-01-17)
- Ava: update Alertmanager grouping and silences doc, land config change (due 2026-01-24)
- Platform Eng: design synthetic canary pipeline options and cost estimate (due 2026-02-07)

Postmortem notes / blameless takeaways:
- We had multiple single points of observability failure (exporters) that cascade into alerting. Investing in simple heartbeat metrics and safe SLO math prevents a large class of noisy incidents.
- Pager noise increases cognitive load; when we detect telemetry instability we should default to graceful-suppression and fast triage to avoid burning precious oncall cycles.
- Improvements should first target detection (heartbeat) + safe math (SLO queries) + notification hygiene (grouping/dedupe).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should missing telemetry for short windows be treated as a warning rather than error for SLO calculations? (tradeoffs for user-facing vs internal metrics)
- Can we automate temporary silencing when heartbeat is absent (silence per-service alerts for the duration of telemetry outage)?
- How much cost does synthetic canary traffic add and where to run it (edge vs internal)?

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Watch for services that still emit high cardinality labels (pod_id, container_sha). Need a removal plan to collapse label space.
- Consider a small middleware shim that emits heartbeat in C++ service runtime (easy for everyone)
- If we implement silence automation, ensure we do not hide real incidents forever -> require human-in-loop confirmation after 15m.

Reference artifacts:
- Incident channel: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02OPS/p1678123456789012
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1423
- Infra PR with temp fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/837

Draft status: this doc is a WIP. I'll update after SRE-1423 merges and we validate heartbeat in staging. Please leave comments inline or add suggestions on the Jira ticket.

-- Ava
